newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Q1 industrial output down 15.4 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Q1 industrial output down 15.4 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Bulgarian industrial output fell a real 15.4 percent in the first quarter of this year against the same period last year, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.

"The industrial production fall in the first quarter of this year was due to the shrinking orders, reduced by soaring inflation and the sharp lev fall against the dollar, which curbed economic activity," a NSI official told a news conference.

Political instability and delayed reforms triggered first quarter cumulative consumer price inflation to 452 percent and March year-on-year inflation was 2,040.5 percent. Producer prices rose 2,072.7 percent year on year in March, NSI figures showed.
The lev slumped to the record lows of 3,000-3,200 per dollar in February from around 500 at the start of the year.

Production of foods, drinks and tobbacco fell by a real 33 percent year on year. Oil processing declined by a real 22 percent. Machine building and electronics posted a fall of 26 percent in the first three months of this year.
State industrial sector's metal ore flotation posted a rise of 40 percent, metallurgy of 10 percent and chemical production of around three percent.
The private industrial sector share in total production was 18 percent. The production of the private sector fell a real six percent year on year.
"This was the first time when the private sector posted a fall in production, which began in February and continued in March," the NSI official added.
The fall was mainly due to the lower output of the private food and beverage industry, which was down around a real 30 percent year on year.

In the first quarter of the year only 15 firms have contributed to around 43 percent of the total production in the industrial sector. 11 of those 15 are of the oil-processing and chemical industries, metallurgy and energy production.
The structure of Bulgaria's industrial production has significantly changed since 1989.

"While in 1989 machine building and electronics and food and beverage industries accounted for more than half of production, in the first quarter of this year chemical, oil processing and metallurgy accounted for 49 percent of industrial output," the official said.
Chemical industry alone accounted for 39 percent of total production in the first quarter.
